history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. This is a prominent LINGAYAT (Veerashaiva) MATHA, a monastic institution, not a temple. Originally located within Chitradurga Fort, it now stands about 2 km northwest of the fort in Chitradurga city. Established in 1703 (per news reports - verify), it inherits the tradition of the 12th-century Sharanas - Allamaprabhu is believed to have been the first president of the Shoonya Peetha (throne of the void) established by Basavanna's Anubhava Mantapa, and the Chitradurga math continues that tradition. Twenty pontiffs from Sri Murige Swamiji-I to the present Shivamurthy Murugha Sharanaru (head since 1991, succeeding Mallikarjuna Murugharajendra Swamiji) have adorned its seat; successive Nayaka rulers of Chitradurga honoured its pontiffs as Rajagurus. It runs 150+ spiritual and academic institutions with 3,000 branches across India and is noted for secular service - grants came from rulers of Keladi, Kodagu, Mysore, Kolhapur and even Muslim Nawabs, and subjects of all communities. COORDINATES ARE APPROXIMATE (geocoder returned a nearby locality, not the matha itself - verify). RECENT CONTROVERSY (verify): since 2022 pontiff Shivamurthy Murugha Sharanaru has faced POCSO and SC/ST Act charges and judicial custody; the Karnataka High Court appointed the Chitradurga district judge as administrator - a developing legal matter, noted here for completeness.
